title: Appendix A — Sunny Side Egg
text: We wanted to explore the CMO dataset to understand the relationship between different commodities of various countries overtime, potentially exploring forecasting models for price prediction.

title: Appendix A — Sunny Side Egg
text:
Reasoning

Research Questions

Matin: What is the effect of fertilizers price on jasmine rice in the south east asian region?


Jospeh: To understand the price changes of arabica, cocoa, robusta with regards to macroeconomic state of the world!


Ari: To understand the effects of crude oil prices impact different groups of commodities in terms of price or price projections.



Reason for Exploration

Group interests in the idea of how macroeconomics affects the world we live in, and our daily lives in regards to food materials.



Communication Policy

We have created a google chat, and we will be meeting every Thursday weekly at 3-4PM for overseeing process.



Roles

Matin: technical assistant and main person of contact; will talk with Amin and preceptors


Ari: technical lead


Joseph: Team Leader



Conflict Resolution

We will adapt to any sudden changes, and if anyone needs help we would offer replacement tasks. Accomodation is key in our group, and we will periodically checkup with each group members with their assigned tasks.

title: Appendix A — Sunny Side Egg
text:
Data

Import


Code
CMO_AnnualPrice <- read_csv("../data/raw/CMO-AnnualPrice.csv")
CMO_AnnualPrice_Real <- read_csv("../data/raw/CMO-AnnualPriceReal.csv")



CMO: Commodity Markets Output



Data Cleaning


Code
CMO_AnnualPrice <- CMO_AnnualPrice[-c(67:77), ] # dropping the empty rows

cmo_clean <- CMO_AnnualPrice_Real %>%
  select(-starts_with("...")) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~na_if(., "…"))) %>%
  mutate(across(-Year, as.numeric)) %>%
  clean_names()




Time Series Data


Code
model_data <- cmo_clean %>%
  select(year, crude_oil_average, urea, rice_thai_5_percent) %>%
  drop_na()

ts_data <- ts(model_data[, c("crude_oil_average", "urea", "rice_thai_5_percent")], 
              start = min(model_data$year), 
              frequency = 1)

10-Year Forecast


Code
forecast_10yr <- predict(var_model, n.ahead = 10, ci = 0.95)

plot(forecast_10yr, 
     names = "rice_thai_5_percent", 
     main = "10-Year Forecast: Benchmark SEA Rice Prices",
     xlab = "Year", 
     ylab = "Real Price ($/mt)")











Impulse Response Function (IRF)


Code
irf_model <- irf(var_model, 
                 impulse = "urea", 
                 response = "rice_thai_5_percent", 
                 n.ahead = 10, 
                 boot = TRUE)

irf_df <- data.frame(
  year_after_shock = 0:10,
  estimate = as.numeric(irf_model$irf$urea),
  lower_ci = as.numeric(irf_model$Lower$urea),
  upper_ci = as.numeric(irf_model$Upper$urea)
)

ggplot(irf_df, aes(x = year_after_shock, y = estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", size = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci), fill = "#D95F02", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(color = "#D95F02", size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#D95F02", size = 3) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", margin = margin(b = 20)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Macroeconomic Shock: Impact of Fertilizer Costs on Mekong Rice",
    subtitle = "Impulse Response Function (VAR Model): Response to a systemic Urea price spike",
    x = "Years Following the Initial Shock",
    y = "Change in Rice Price ($/mt)",
    caption = "Proxy applied for Cambodian Rice Markets | 95% Bootstrap CI"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 10, 2))

title: Appendix B — Case Study
text:
Color

The color scheme used are on the brighter sides. Texts are distinguishable from the plots, headers and title are bolded and in huge font which set asides the paragraph from other paragraphs. Not sure if the color is made using scale_viridis, however it does look distinguishable enough so that there’s accomadation for those with color disabilities. Captions and subtitles are greyed and lower opacity, which means the center of attention remains on the plot.


Color contrasts, used in the plot is used cleverly to create extreme contrasts, and buffer texts within the labels, using white space, or negative space. The overall theme is very clean and minimal. Furthermore, color association is used cleverly as well, for example far left being blue green, and far right being more red pigments.

title: Appendix B — Case Study
text:
Kinds of Plots

The title of the plot does giveaway some of idea of what kind of plots that would be used to support the data story. Furthermore, in each visualization group, **there’s a reference image in no color which is used cleverly as a control, or for users to look back and forth to know the context. For example, dividing the country to different regions, but the colors are representative.

title: Appendix B — Case Study
text:
Fonts

The font used is clean and in a pair. There’s san seriff and seriff font pair which is the standard in NYT. This offers more distinction between the titles, subtitles and labels, but the paragraph denoting the story itself is seperated.
